summary: EarthPulse is an interactive web app that helps people explore how vegetation, precipitation, and air temperature change over time. Users choose a variable, a date range, and up to four areas on a map. EarthPulse retrieves monthly observations, displays time-series charts, and estimates trend direction and magnitude using the Mann–Kendall test and Sen’s slope. Its plain-language results make Earth science data easier to explore and understand.
details:
EarthPulse addresses the “Be An Earth System Trend Detective!” challenge by making it easier to explore changes in Earth system variables across different places and time periods.

Users select a variable and date range, then draw up to four rectangular areas on an interactive map. The backend retrieves and processes the data into monthly observations. For each area, the app displays a time-series chart, data coverage, source information, and a plain-language trend summary. It uses the Mann–Kendall test and Sen’s slope to describe trends; statistical significance does not imply causation.

For vegetation, EarthPulse uses Terra MODIS MOD13Q1 Collection 6.1 NDVI data accessed through Microsoft Planetary Computer. It filters observations using the product’s pixel-quality data and creates monthly regional estimates. Temperature and precipitation are retrieved through the Meteomatics Weather API using ERA5 and CHIRPS data products, respectively.

EarthPulse is built with React and TypeScript, Leaflet, Python, and FastAPI. It is designed as an educational tool for students and the public to ask questions about environmental change and explore the evidence behind the results
dataRefs: NASA Terra MODIS Vegetation Indices (MOD13Q1 Collection 6.1)
